# What You Didn’t Know About ‘I Can Only Imagine’s’ Lead Actor, J.Michael Finley
## Casting J.Michael Finley in the Role of Bart Millard
Choosing who to play Bart took time, but when the crew found J. Michael Finley, they knew it was meant to be.
“We found [Finely] on Broadway”, says Downes. “He was playing the role of John Valjean in Les Miserables. We thought, ‘is this kid for real?’
“So we put him through an audition process and what we found out was that he’s a Baptist preachers kid, from Middle America, who grew up going to Mercy Me concerts. We thought, ‘You’re too good to be true’.”
With the perfect cast, including Dennis Quaid as Bart’s Dad, the producers felt they had a responsibility to honour the original intention of the song, and make sure its heart was well told in the movie.
> “He’s a Baptist preachers kid, from middle-America, who grew up going to Mercy Me concerts. We thought, ‘You’re too good to be true’.”
“Many people say that when they first heard the song they had this tremendous rush of hope, and this picture of what Heaven could be like. So we do the same thing with the movie; the movie paints this picture of a tremendous rush of hope at the end of the film and some people have said it’s one of the most brilliant endings they’ve ever seen—which is certainly very high remarks, but we’re very happy with it.”
Asked how he thinks anyone could forgive someone who’d wronged them as much as Bart’s Dad did him, Downes says, “I don’t know. For what Bart went through to all of a sudden just say, ‘You know what Dad, I completely forgive you’, what Bart would say is, ‘it was only God, and God deserves all the credit because the work that Jesus Christ did on the cross was sufficient’. That it was the Holy Spirit in him that allowed him to do that.”
_I Can Only Imagine_ is in cinemas March 15.

After Arthur's funeral, Bart rejoins the band and writes "I Can Only Imagine", and also calls Shannon and apologizes to her for the first time since their breakup. Brickell sends the demo tape to several artists, including Grant, who, deeply moved by the song, asks to record it herself as her next single, and Bart, who just wants the song to be heard, accepts. The band releases the song as their first single, achieving success on both Christian and mainstream radio.

The film was announced in December 2016.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/I_Can_Only_Imagine_(film)#cite_note-oklahoma-9) Dennis Quaid joined the cast in January 2017.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/I_Can_Only_Imagine_(film)#cite_note-Deadline1517-10)Broadway actor J. Michael Finley, who sang all the songs in the movie, makes his film debut as Bart Millard.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/I_Can_Only_Imagine_(film)#cite_note-deadline81417-1) The same month, it was announced that the film was slated for release in the spring of 2018.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/I_Can_Only_Imagine_(film)#cite_note-Deadline1517-10) In August 2017, Lionsgate and Roadside Attractions signed on as distributors for the film for a nationwide release in the United States.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/I_Can_Only_Imagine_(film)#cite_note-deadline81417-1)[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/I_Can_Only_Imagine_(film)#cite_note-11)

_I Can Only Imagine_ was released on March 16, 2018, alongside _Tomb Raider_ and _Love, Simon_, and was originally projected to gross $2–4 million from 1,620 theaters in its opening weekend.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/I_Can_Only_Imagine_(film)#cite_note-preview-13) However, after making $6.2 million on its first day (including $1.3 million from Thursday night previews), weekend estimates were increased to $14 million.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/I_Can_Only_Imagine_(film)#cite_note-opening-14) It ended up grossing $17.1 million, exceeding expectations and finishing third at the box office behind _Black Panther_ and _Tomb Raider_. 67% of the opening weekend audience was female while 80% was over the age of 35.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/I_Can_Only_Imagine_(film)#cite_note-opening2-15) It was the fourth best-ever opening for a faith-based film, following _The Passion of the Christ_ ($83.8 million), _Son of God_ ($25.6 million) and _Heaven Is for Real_ ($22.5 million).[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/I_Can_Only_Imagine_(film)#cite_note-16) In its second weekend the film was added to 624 additional theaters and dropped just 19% to $13.8 million, again finishing third.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/I_Can_Only_Imagine_(film)#cite_note-17) It was added to another 395 venues and finished fourth in its third weekend, making $10.4 million (including $3 million on Easter Sunday).[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/I_Can_Only_Imagine_(film)#cite_note-18)
The film has been translated and distributed in several countries,[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/I_Can_Only_Imagine_(film)#cite_note-19) including China, according to co-director Jon Erwin:

Choosing who to play Bart took time, but when the crew found J. Michael Finley, they knew it was meant to be.
“We found [Finely] on Broadway”, says Downes. “He was playing the role of John Valjean in Les Miserables. We thought, ‘is this kid for real?’
“So we put him through an audition process and what we found out was that he’s a Baptist preachers kid, from Middle America, who grew up going to Mercy Me concerts. We thought, ‘You’re too good to be true’.”
With the perfect cast, including Dennis Quaid as Bart’s Dad, the producers felt they had a responsibility to honour the original intention of the song, and make sure its heart was well told in the movie.
> “He’s a Baptist preachers kid, from middle-America, who grew up going to Mercy Me concerts. We thought, ‘You’re too good to be true’.”
“Many people say that when they first heard the song they had this tremendous rush of hope, and this picture of what Heaven could be like. So we do the same thing with the movie; the movie paints this picture of a tremendous rush of hope at the end of the film and some people have said it’s one of the most brilliant endings they’ve ever seen—which is certainly very high remarks, but we’re very happy with it.”
Asked how he thinks anyone could forgive someone who’d wronged them as much as Bart’s Dad did him, Downes says, “I don’t know. For what Bart went through to all of a sudden just say, ‘You know what Dad, I completely forgive you’, what Bart would say is, ‘it was only God, and God deserves all the credit because the work that Jesus Christ did on the cross was sufficient’. That it was the Holy Spirit in him that allowed him to do that.”
_I Can Only Imagine_ is in cinemas March 15.

## J. MICHAEL FINLEY
##### Bart Millard
J. Michael Finley made his Broadway debut in **Les Miserables** in 2014, and is making his screen-acting debut in **I CAN ONLY IMAGINE**. His stage credits include playing Steve in **Hair** (at the Paramount Theatre), **Sweeney Todd** (at the Drury Lane Theatre) and Louie in **The Christmas Schooner** (in the Mercury Theater). After production wrapped on **I CAN ONLY IMAGINE**, J. Michael returned to Broadway.
texts.1:
## DENNIS QUAID
##### Arthur Millard
Dennis Quaid was born in Houston to Juanita Bonniedale, a real-estate agent, and William Rudy Quaid, an electrician. He grew up in the Houston suburb of Bellaire. He was raised a Baptist, and studied drama, Mandarin Chinese, and dance while a student at Bellaire High School. He continued his study at the University of Houston but dropped out before completing his degree. He moved to Los Angeles to pursue a film career where his brother, Randy Quaid, had already begun to build a successful career. However, Dennis initially had trouble finding film roles, but began to gain notice when he appeared in **Breaking Away** in 1979. He earned strong reviews for his role in **The Right Stuff**. Among his many other roles are the recent television series **American Crime Story** and the movie **A Dog’s Purpose**. Aside from acting, Quaid is also a musician and plays with his band, The Sharks. He also holds a flying license and is a five-handicap golfer.

##### Mrs. Fincher
Priscilla Shirer is a wife and mom first, but put a Bible in her hand and a message in her heart, and you’ll see why thousands meet God in powerful, personal ways at her conferences and through her books and Bible studies. She and her husband Jerry lead Going Beyond Ministries, thorough which they provide spiritual support and resources to the body of Christ. Between writing and studying, Priscilla can usually be found at home cleaning up after (and trying to satisfy the appetites of) her three rapidly growing boys. Priscilla played Elizabeth in the powerful movie **War Room**.

## MADELINE CARROLL
##### Shannon
Madeline Carroll began modeling when she was 3-years old after being “discovered” in a nail shop in Sherman Oaks, California. She has performed in 65 national commercials, and has guest-starred on several TV shows and series. Her favorite roles have been as Julie Baker in **Flipped**, and Molly in **Swing Vote**. She is active in giving to the foundation Zoe International, a non-profit Christian organization that rescues children from child prostitution. She also volunteers at The Dream Center and partners with her family in feeding the homeless every Tuesday night.

## TRACE ADKINS
##### Brickell
**I CAN ONLY IMAGINE** is Trace Adkins’ second film with the Erwin Brothers and Kevin Downes after starring as Bones in **Moms’ Night Out**. Trace's trademark baritone has powered countless hits to the top of the charts and turned albums into Platinum plaques, selling more than 10 million albums cumulatively. The Grammy-nominated member of the Grand Ole Opry is also a television personality, actor, and author. He’s also a spokesman for the Wounded Warrior Program and the American Red Cross, and he has performed seven USO Tours. He authored his autobiography, _A Personal Stand_, in 2007 and was a finalist in the 2008 version of NBC's **The Celebrity Apprentice**. Trace played a tough-as-nails biker in **The Lincoln Lawyer**, he developed and hosted GAC's **Great American Heroes** series to pay tribute to everyday Americans doing great things, and he has hosted the American Country Awards on FOX. Trace will soon be seen in the feature film **Hickok**.

## CLORIS LEACHMAN
##### Memaw
A true Hollywood icon, fan favorite Cloris Leachman has won an Oscar, a record-setting eight Primetime Emmy Awards, and a Daytime Emmy. In 2005, at age 82, she appeared on **Dancing with the Stars**. Born in Des Moines, Iowa, she moved to New York to pursue an acting career. She appeared in many television anthologies and series through the 1950s and 1960s with a handful of films, including **Kiss Me Deadly, The Rack, The Chapman Report**, and **Butch Cassidy And The Sundance Kid**. Though she won an Oscar for **The Last Picture Show** in 1971 and appeared in three Mel Brooks movies, her career remained mainly in television. Cloris won two Emmys for her work on **The Mary Tyler Moore Show**and the spin-off series **Phyllis**, for which she also won a Golden Globe Award. Her first Emmy was in 1973 for the television movie **A Brand New Life**. She also won two Emmys as a supporting player for **Malcolm in the Middle**. Cloris is 90-years young and not slowing down. She can be seen on the cable series **American Gods**.

_I Can Only Imagine_ was released on March 16, 2018, alongside _Tomb Raider_ and _Love, Simon_, and was originally projected to gross $2–4 million from 1,620 theaters in its opening weekend.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/I_Can_Only_Imagine_(film)#cite_note-preview-13) However, after making $6.2 million on its first day (including $1.3 million from Thursday night previews), weekend estimates were increased to $14 million.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/I_Can_Only_Imagine_(film)#cite_note-opening-14) It ended up grossing $17.1 million, exceeding expectations and finishing third at the box office behind _Black Panther_ and _Tomb Raider_. 67% of the opening weekend audience was female while 80% was over the age of 35.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/I_Can_Only_Imagine_(film)#cite_note-opening2-15) It was the fourth best-ever opening for a faith-based film, following _The Passion of the Christ_ ($83.8 million), _Son of God_ ($25.6 million) and _Heaven Is for Real_ ($22.5 million).[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/I_Can_Only_Imagine_(film)#cite_note-16) In its second weekend the film was added to 624 additional theaters and dropped just 19% to $13.8 million, again finishing third.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/I_Can_Only_Imagine_(film)#cite_note-17) It was added to another 395 venues and finished fourth in its third weekend, making $10.4 million (including $3 million on Easter Sunday).[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/I_Can_Only_Imagine_(film)#cite_note-18)

On review aggregatorRotten Tomatoes, the film holds an approval rating of 69% based on 32 reviews, with an average rating of 5.8/10. The website's critical consensus reads, "_I Can Only Imagine_'s message will have the most impact among Christian audiences, but overall, its performances and storytelling represent a notable evolution in faith-based cinema."[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/I_Can_Only_Imagine_(film)#cite_note-21) However, on Metacritic, the film has a weighted average score of 30 out of 100, based on eight critics, indicating "generally unfavorable" reviews.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/I_Can_Only_Imagine_(film)#cite_note-22) Audiences polled by CinemaScore gave the film a rare average grade of "A+" on an A+ to F scale.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/I_Can_Only_Imagine_(film)#cite_note-opening-14)

_The Arizona Republic_'s James Ward gave the film 4 stars out of 5 and wrote, "Too often faith-based films—say anything with Kirk Cameron or the terrible _[God's Not Dead](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/God's\_Not\_Dead\_(film\_series) "God's Not Dead (film series)")_ series—tend to preach to the choir or hector their audience. The Erwins' films—_I Can Only Imagine_ definitely among them—are more inclusive, charitable of spirit and hopeful, all qualities that are always appreciated, be they rooted in Christian faith or otherwise."[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/I_Can_Only_Imagine_(film)#cite_note-23) David Ehrlich of IndieWire gave the film a "C−" saying: "There's a reason why all of these movies are so amateurishly made; why they all end with links to religious websites; why they all look like they were shot on an iPhone by a Walmart-brand Janusz Kaminski who lit each interior like the white light of heaven was streaming through every window... Art can be affirmation, but affirmation cannot be art."[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/I_Can_Only_Imagine_(film)#cite_note-24)
Faith-based reviewers mostly gave the movie positive reviews. Megan Basham of _World_ magazine called Quaid "the real workhorse" and added that he "bears the heavy load of convincingly giving us both a monster and a repentant dad longing to connect with his son. Quaid impresses on both counts."[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/I_Can_Only_Imagine_(film)#cite_note-25) Michael Foust of the _Southern Baptist Texan_ gave the film 5 out of 5 stars and wrote, "The screenplay is gripping, the soundtrack is perfect, and the performances by Quaid and Finley had me squirming, laughing and crying."[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/I_Can_Only_Imagine_(film)#cite_note-26)

The film was released on iTunes and Google Play on June 5, 2018, and on DVD and Blu-ray on June 12, 2018.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/I_Can_Only_Imagine_(film)#cite_note-27)[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/I_Can_Only_Imagine_(film)#cite_note-28)_I Can Only Imagine_ was the no. 1 film in DVD sales and rentals for the weeks ending June 17 and June 24, 2018.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/I_Can_Only_Imagine_(film)#cite_note-29)[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/I_Can_Only_Imagine_(film)#cite_note-30) As of February 2020, _I Can Only Imagine_ has earned $24 million in home media sales.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/I_Can_Only_Imagine_(film)#cite_note-TN-4)

# What You Didn’t Know About ‘I Can Only Imagine’s’ Lead Actor, J.Michael Finley
## Casting J.Michael Finley in the Role of Bart Millard
Choosing who to play Bart took time, but when the crew found J. Michael Finley, they knew it was meant to be.
“We found [Finely] on Broadway”, says Downes. “He was playing the role of John Valjean in Les Miserables. We thought, ‘is this kid for real?’
“So we put him through an audition process and what we found out was that he’s a Baptist preachers kid, from Middle America, who grew up going to Mercy Me concerts. We thought, ‘You’re too good to be true’.”
With the perfect cast, including Dennis Quaid as Bart’s Dad, the producers felt they had a responsibility to honour the original intention of the song, and make sure its heart was well told in the movie.
> “He’s a Baptist preachers kid, from middle-America, who grew up going to Mercy Me concerts. We thought, ‘You’re too good to be true’.”
“Many people say that when they first heard the song they had this tremendous rush of hope, and this picture of what Heaven could be like. So we do the same thing with the movie; the movie paints this picture of a tremendous rush of hope at the end of the film and some people have said it’s one of the most brilliant endings they’ve ever seen—which is certainly very high remarks, but we’re very happy with it.”
Asked how he thinks anyone could forgive someone who’d wronged them as much as Bart’s Dad did him, Downes says, “I don’t know. For what Bart went through to all of a sudden just say, ‘You know what Dad, I completely forgive you’, what Bart would say is, ‘it was only God, and God deserves all the credit because the work that Jesus Christ did on the cross was sufficient’. That it was the Holy Spirit in him that allowed him to do that.”

## J. MICHAEL FINLEY
##### Bart Millard
J. Michael Finley made his Broadway debut in **Les Miserables** in 2014, and is making his screen-acting debut in **I CAN ONLY IMAGINE**. His stage credits include playing Steve in **Hair** (at the Paramount Theatre), **Sweeney Todd** (at the Drury Lane Theatre) and Louie in **The Christmas Schooner** (in the Mercury Theater). After production wrapped on **I CAN ONLY IMAGINE**, J. Michael returned to Broadway.

## DENNIS QUAID
##### Arthur Millard
Dennis Quaid was born in Houston to Juanita Bonniedale, a real-estate agent, and William Rudy Quaid, an electrician. He grew up in the Houston suburb of Bellaire. He was raised a Baptist, and studied drama, Mandarin Chinese, and dance while a student at Bellaire High School. He continued his study at the University of Houston but dropped out before completing his degree. He moved to Los Angeles to pursue a film career where his brother, Randy Quaid, had already begun to build a successful career. However, Dennis initially had trouble finding film roles, but began to gain notice when he appeared in **Breaking Away** in 1979. He earned strong reviews for his role in **The Right Stuff**. Among his many other roles are the recent television series **American Crime Story** and the movie **A Dog’s Purpose**. Aside from acting, Quaid is also a musician and plays with his band, The Sharks. He also holds a flying license and is a five-handicap golfer.

## PRISCILLA SHIRER
##### Mrs. Fincher
Priscilla Shirer is a wife and mom first, but put a Bible in her hand and a message in her heart, and you’ll see why thousands meet God in powerful, personal ways at her conferences and through her books and Bible studies. She and her husband Jerry lead Going Beyond Ministries, thorough which they provide spiritual support and resources to the body of Christ. Between writing and studying, Priscilla can usually be found at home cleaning up after (and trying to satisfy the appetites of) her three rapidly growing boys. Priscilla played Elizabeth in the powerful movie **War Room**.

## MADELINE CARROLL
##### Shannon
Madeline Carroll began modeling when she was 3-years old after being “discovered” in a nail shop in Sherman Oaks, California. She has performed in 65 national commercials, and has guest-starred on several TV shows and series. Her favorite roles have been as Julie Baker in **Flipped**, and Molly in **Swing Vote**. She is active in giving to the foundation Zoe International, a non-profit Christian organization that rescues children from child prostitution. She also volunteers at The Dream Center and partners with her family in feeding the homeless every Tuesday night.

## TRACE ADKINS
##### Brickell
**I CAN ONLY IMAGINE** is Trace Adkins’ second film with the Erwin Brothers and Kevin Downes after starring as Bones in **Moms’ Night Out**. Trace's trademark baritone has powered countless hits to the top of the charts and turned albums into Platinum plaques, selling more than 10 million albums cumulatively. The Grammy-nominated member of the Grand Ole Opry is also a television personality, actor, and author. He’s also a spokesman for the Wounded Warrior Program and the American Red Cross, and he has performed seven USO Tours. He authored his autobiography, _A Personal Stand_, in 2007 and was a finalist in the 2008 version of NBC's **The Celebrity Apprentice**. Trace played a tough-as-nails biker in **The Lincoln Lawyer**, he developed and hosted GAC's **Great American Heroes** series to pay tribute to everyday Americans doing great things, and he has hosted the American Country Awards on FOX. Trace will soon be seen in the feature film **Hickok**.

## CLORIS LEACHMAN
##### Memaw
A true Hollywood icon, fan favorite Cloris Leachman has won an Oscar, a record-setting eight Primetime Emmy Awards, and a Daytime Emmy. In 2005, at age 82, she appeared on **Dancing with the Stars**. Born in Des Moines, Iowa, she moved to New York to pursue an acting career. She appeared in many television anthologies and series through the 1950s and 1960s with a handful of films, including **Kiss Me Deadly, The Rack, The Chapman Report**, and **Butch Cassidy And The Sundance Kid**. Though she won an Oscar for **The Last Picture Show** in 1971 and appeared in three Mel Brooks movies, her career remained mainly in television. Cloris won two Emmys for her work on **The Mary Tyler Moore Show**and the spin-off series **Phyllis**, for which she also won a Golden Globe Award. Her first Emmy was in 1973 for the television movie **A Brand New Life**. She also won two Emmys as a supporting player for **Malcolm in the Middle**. Cloris is 90-years young and not slowing down. She can be seen on the cable series **American Gods**.

Dennis Quaid and Laura Savoie have never let their 39-year age difference define their relationship.
The couple met at a business event in 2019 and married in an intimate seaside ceremony the following year. Dennis was 66, while Laura was 27.
Six years later, they remain together and also work side by side through the production company they co-founded. Quaid has described Laura as the love of his life and called their marriage the closest relationship he has ever experienced.
Do you believe age matters when two people have found the right connection?

_**I Can Only Imagine**_ is a 2018 American Christianbiographicaldrama film directed by the Erwin Brothers and written by Alex Cramer, Jon Erwin, and Brent McCorkle, based on the story behind the group MercyMe's song of the same name, one of the best-selling Christian singles of all time.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/I_Can_Only_Imagine_(film)#cite_note-5) The film stars J. Michael Finley as Bart Millard, the lead singer who wrote the song about his relationship with his father Arthur Millard (Dennis Quaid). Madeline Carroll, Trace Adkins, Priscilla Shirer, and Cloris Leachman also star.
_I Can Only Imagine_ was released in the United States on March 16, 2018. It was a box office success, grossing $86 million worldwide against a production budget of $7 million, earning more than twelve times its budget. It is the fifth highest-grossing music biopic[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/I_Can_Only_Imagine_(film)#cite_note-6) and sixth highest-grossing Christian film[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/I_Can_Only_Imagine_(film)#cite_note-7) of all-time in the United States. At the 2018 Dove Awards, the film won "Inspirational Film of the Year".[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/I_Can_Only_Imagine_(film)#cite_note-doveawards.com-8) A sequel, _I Can Only Imagine 2_, was released on February 20, 2026.
Ten-year-old Bart Millard lives with his mother Adele and abusive father Arthur in Texas. One day, Bart's mother drops him off at a Christian camp, where Bart meets Shannon Street. Upon his return from camp, Bart finds that his mother has left and movers are removing her belongings. Bart angrily confronts Arthur, who denies that his abusiveness was the reason she left.

Years later, in high school, Bart and Shannon are dating. Bart plays football to please Arthur, but is injured, breaking both ankles and ending his career. The only elective with openings is music class, so he reluctantly signs up. Initially, Bart is assigned to be a sound technician, but after overhearing him singing, the director casts him in the lead role in the school production of _Oklahoma!_. Bart overcomes his reluctance and gives an impressive performance, but does not tell Arthur, who finds out the night of the show when he happens to see a flyer for the show in a diner. Arthur suddenly collapses in pain, and finds out he has cancer, which he hides from Bart. The following morning, Bart fights with Arthur, who smashes a plate over his head. At church, Shannon sees the blood and presses Bart to open up, but he responds by breaking up with her, and leaves town to seek his fortune in the city.
Bart joins a band in need of a singer, and convinces Christian music producer Scott Brickell to manage the band and secure a showcase in Nashville. Bart surprises Shannon and invites her to tour with the band, and is confused when Shannon flatly refuses. In Nashville, Brickell introduces Bart to established artists Amy Grant and Michael W. Smith, but is unable to convince record executives to sign the band, who do not believe the band, now performing as "MercyMe", is good enough. Devastated, Bart quits the band, but Brickell thinks that Bart needs to resolve issues in his personal life, so Bart reconciles with the band and asks them to wait for him, and leaves to return home.
Bart returns home late at night, and is confused to find that Arthur has prepared breakfast for him the next morning. Arthur claims to have become a Christian, but Bart is skeptical and refuses to forgive him, and leaves. In anger and despair, Arthur smashes his old Jeep, which he had asked Bart to help him restore. Bart attempts to drive away in Arthur's pickup, but discovers his father's terminal cancer diagnosis, and returns to Arthur. Bart forgives his father, and the two form a deep bond, but Arthur soon dies of his illness.

After Arthur's funeral, Bart rejoins the band and writes "I Can Only Imagine", and also calls Shannon and apologizes to her for the first time since their breakup. Brickell sends the demo tape to several artists, including Grant, who, deeply moved by the song, asks to record it herself as her next single, and Bart, who just wants the song to be heard, accepts. On stage, Grant begins the song, but can't bring herself to sing it, and calls Bart on stage from the audience to sing it himself. After Bart's performance, he sees his father in the audience smiling and clapping. The audience gives an enthusiastic ovation, and he reunites with Shannon, who was also in attendance. The band releases the song as their first single, achieving success on both Christian and mainstream radio.

Michael Finley, who sang all the songs in the movie, makes his film debut as Bart Millard.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/I_Can_Only_Imagine_(film)#cite_note-deadline81417-1) The same month, it was announced that the film was slated for release in the spring of 2018.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/I_Can_Only_Imagine_(film)#cite_note-Deadline1517-10) In August 2017, Lionsgate and Roadside Attractions signed on as distributors for the film for a nationwide release in the United States.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/I_Can_Only_Imagine_(film)#cite_note-deadline81417-1)[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/I_Can_Only_Imagine_(film)#cite_note-11)
_I Can Only Imagine_ grossed $83.4 million in the United States and Canada and $1.8 million in other territories, for a worldwide total of $85.2 million, against a production budget of $7 million.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/I_Can_Only_Imagine_(film)#cite_note-TN-4) It is the highest-grossing independent film of 2018.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/I_Can_Only_Imagine_(film)#cite_note-12)

_I Can Only Imagine_ was released on March 16, 2018, alongside _Tomb Raider_ and _Love, Simon_, and was originally projected to gross $2–4 million from 1,620 theaters in its opening weekend.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/I_Can_Only_Imagine_(film)#cite_note-preview-13) However, after making $6.2 million on its first day (including $1.3 million from Thursday night previews), weekend estimates were increased to $14 million.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/I_Can_Only_Imagine_(film)#cite_note-opening-14) It ended up grossing $17.1 million, exceeding expectations and finishing third at the box office behind _Black Panther_ and _Tomb Raider_. 67% of the opening weekend audience was female while 80% was over the age of 35.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/I_Can_Only_Imagine_(film)#cite_note-opening2-15) It was the fourth best-ever opening for a faith-based film, following _The Passion of the Christ_ ($83.8 million), _Son of God_ ($25.6 million) and _Heaven Is for Real_ ($22.5 million).[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/I_Can_Only_Imagine_(film)#cite_note-16) In its second weekend the film was added to 624 additional theaters and dropped just 19% to $13.8 million, again finishing third.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/I_Can_Only_Imagine_(film)#cite_note-17) It was added to another 395 venues and finished fourth in its third weekend, making $10.4 million (including $3 million on Easter Sunday).[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/I_Can_Only_Imagine_(film)#cite_note-18)
The film has been translated and distributed in several countries,[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/I_Can_Only_Imagine_(film)#cite_note-19) including China, according to co-director Jon Erwin:

> I find it very interesting that in the same year that China actually restricted ... Christianity, they paid for "I Can Only Imagine". ... They paid for the right to translate it and distribute it to their people. That's happened in over 100 countries around the world with our films.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/I_Can_Only_Imagine_(film)#cite_note-20)
On review aggregatorRotten Tomatoes, the film holds an approval rating of 69% based on 32 reviews, with an average rating of 5.8/10. The website's critical consensus reads, "_I Can Only Imagine_'s message will have the most impact among Christian audiences, but overall, its performances and storytelling represent a notable evolution in faith-based cinema."[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/I_Can_Only_Imagine_(film)#cite_note-21) However, on Metacritic, the film has a weighted average score of 30 out of 100, based on eight critics, indicating "generally unfavorable" reviews.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/I_Can_Only_Imagine_(film)#cite_note-22) Audiences polled by CinemaScore gave the film a rare average grade of "A+" on an A+ to F scale.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/I_Can_Only_Imagine_(film)#cite_note-opening-14)

MercyMe's lead singer, Bart Millard, whose story is told in "I Can Only Imagine" and its sequel, is pictured as an adult with his mother, Adele, and as a child (inset, bottom) in the 1980s. After his mother endured years of emotional abuse, she left Bart's father out of fear for her own life. Bart remained with his father, enduring both physical and emotional abuse. In 2018, Bart made peace with his mother over his difficult childhood. She attended the "I Can Only Imagine" premiere with him and loved the movie, telling him, "I was so scared for my life and I'm so glad that we have each other now." Adele passed away four years later in July 2022.

texts.1:
_**I Can Only Imagine**_ is a 2018 American Christianbiographicaldrama film directed by the Erwin Brothers and written by Alex Cramer, Jon Erwin, and Brent McCorkle, based on the story behind the group MercyMe's song of the same name, one of the best-selling Christian singles of all time.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/I_Can_Only_Imagine_(film)#cite_note-5) The film stars J. Michael Finley as Bart Millard, the lead singer who wrote the song about his relationship with his father Arthur Millard (Dennis Quaid). Madeline Carroll, Trace Adkins, Priscilla Shirer, and Cloris Leachman also star.
_I Can Only Imagine_ was released in the United States on March 16, 2018. It was a box office success, grossing $86 million worldwide against a production budget of $7 million, earning more than twelve times its budget. It is the fifth highest-grossing music biopic[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/I_Can_Only_Imagine_(film)#cite_note-6) and sixth highest-grossing Christian film[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/I_Can_Only_Imagine_(film)#cite_note-7) of all-time in the United States. At the 2018 Dove Awards, the film won "Inspirational Film of the Year".[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/I_Can_Only_Imagine_(film)#cite_note-doveawards.com-8) A sequel, _I Can Only Imagine 2_, was released on February 20, 2026.
Ten-year-old Bart Millard lives with his mother Adele and abusive father Arthur in Texas. One day, Bart's mother drops him off at a Christian camp, where Bart meets Shannon Street. Upon his return from camp, Bart finds that his mother has left and movers are removing her belongings. Bart angrily confronts Arthur, who denies that his abusiveness was the reason she left.
texts.2:
Years later, in high school, Bart and Shannon are dating. Bart plays football to please Arthur, but is injured, breaking both ankles and ending his career. The only elective with openings is music class, so he reluctantly signs up. Initially, Bart is assigned to be a sound technician, but after overhearing him singing, the director casts him in the lead role in the school production of _Oklahoma!_. Bart overcomes his reluctance and gives an impressive performance, but does not tell Arthur, who finds out the night of the show when he happens to see a flyer for the show in a diner. Arthur suddenly collapses in pain, and finds out he has cancer, which he hides from Bart. The following morning, Bart fights with Arthur, who smashes a plate over his head. At church, Shannon sees the blood and presses Bart to open up, but he responds by breaking up with her, and leaves town to seek his fortune in the city.
Bart joins a band in need of a singer, and convinces Christian music producer Scott Brickell to manage the band and secure a showcase in Nashville. Bart surprises Shannon and invites her to tour with the band, and is confused when Shannon flatly refuses. In Nashville, Brickell introduces Bart to established artists Amy Grant and Michael W. Smith, but is unable to convince record executives to sign the band, who do not believe the band, now performing as "MercyMe", is good enough. Devastated, Bart quits the band, but Brickell thinks that Bart needs to resolve issues in his personal life, so Bart reconciles with the band and asks them to wait for him, and leaves to return home.
Bart returns home late at night, and is confused to find that Arthur has prepared breakfast for him the next morning. Arthur claims to have become a Christian, but Bart is skeptical and refuses to forgive him, and leaves. In anger and despair, Arthur smashes his old Jeep, which he had asked Bart to help him restore. Bart attempts to drive away in Arthur's pickup, but discovers his father's terminal cancer diagnosis, and returns to Arthur. Bart forgives his father, and the two form a deep bond, but Arthur soon dies of his illness.
texts.3:
After Arthur's funeral, Bart rejoins the band and writes "I Can Only Imagine", and also calls Shannon and apologizes to her for the first time since their breakup. Brickell sends the demo tape to several artists, including Grant, who, deeply moved by the song, asks to record it herself as her next single, and Bart, who just wants the song to be heard, accepts. On stage, Grant begins the song, but can't bring herself to sing it, and calls Bart on stage from the audience to sing it himself. After Bart's performance, he sees his father in the audience smiling and clapping. The audience gives an enthusiastic ovation, and he reunites with Shannon, who was also in attendance. The band releases the song as their first single, achieving success on both Christian and mainstream radio.

Michael Finley, who sang all the songs in the movie, makes his film debut as Bart Millard.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/I_Can_Only_Imagine_(film)#cite_note-deadline81417-1) The same month, it was announced that the film was slated for release in the spring of 2018.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/I_Can_Only_Imagine_(film)#cite_note-Deadline1517-10) In August 2017, Lionsgate and Roadside Attractions signed on as distributors for the film for a nationwide release in the United States.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/I_Can_Only_Imagine_(film)#cite_note-deadline81417-1)[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/I_Can_Only_Imagine_(film)#cite_note-11)
_I Can Only Imagine_ grossed $83.4 million in the United States and Canada and $1.8 million in other territories, for a worldwide total of $85.2 million, against a production budget of $7 million.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/I_Can_Only_Imagine_(film)#cite_note-TN-4) It is the highest-grossing independent film of 2018.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/I_Can_Only_Imagine_(film)#cite_note-12)
texts.5:
_I Can Only Imagine_ was released on March 16, 2018, alongside _Tomb Raider_ and _Love, Simon_, and was originally projected to gross $2–4 million from 1,620 theaters in its opening weekend.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/I_Can_Only_Imagine_(film)#cite_note-preview-13) However, after making $6.2 million on its first day (including $1.3 million from Thursday night previews), weekend estimates were increased to $14 million.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/I_Can_Only_Imagine_(film)#cite_note-opening-14) It ended up grossing $17.1 million, exceeding expectations and finishing third at the box office behind _Black Panther_ and _Tomb Raider_. 67% of the opening weekend audience was female while 80% was over the age of 35.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/I_Can_Only_Imagine_(film)#cite_note-opening2-15) It was the fourth best-ever opening for a faith-based film, following _The Passion of the Christ_ ($83.8 million), _Son of God_ ($25.6 million) and _Heaven Is for Real_ ($22.5 million).[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/I_Can_Only_Imagine_(film)#cite_note-16) In its second weekend the film was added to 624 additional theaters and dropped just 19% to $13.8 million, again finishing third.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/I_Can_Only_Imagine_(film)#cite_note-17) It was added to another 395 venues and finished fourth in its third weekend, making $10.4 million (including $3 million on Easter Sunday).[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/I_Can_Only_Imagine_(film)#cite_note-18)
The film has been translated and distributed in several countries,[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/I_Can_Only_Imagine_(film)#cite_note-19) including China, according to co-director Jon Erwin:
texts.6:
> I find it very interesting that in the same year that China actually restricted ... Christianity, they paid for "I Can Only Imagine". ... They paid for the right to translate it and distribute it to their people. That's happened in over 100 countries around the world with our films.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/I_Can_Only_Imagine_(film)#cite_note-20)
On review aggregatorRotten Tomatoes, the film holds an approval rating of 69% based on 32 reviews, with an average rating of 5.8/10. The website's critical consensus reads, "_I Can Only Imagine_'s message will have the most impact among Christian audiences, but overall, its performances and storytelling represent a notable evolution in faith-based cinema."[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/I_Can_Only_Imagine_(film)#cite_note-21) However, on Metacritic, the film has a weighted average score of 30 out of 100, based on eight critics, indicating "generally unfavorable" reviews.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/I_Can_Only_Imagine_(film)#cite_note-22) Audiences polled by CinemaScore gave the film a rare average grade of "A+" on an A+ to F scale.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/I_Can_Only_Imagine_(film)#cite_note-opening-14)

MercyMe's lead singer, Bart Millard, whose story is told in "I Can Only Imagine" and its sequel, is pictured as an adult with his mother, Adele, and as a child (inset, bottom) in the 1980s. After his mother endured years of emotional abuse, she left Bart's father out of fear for her own life. Bart remained with his father, enduring both physical and emotional abuse. In 2018, Bart made peace with his mother over his difficult childhood. She attended the "I Can Only Imagine" premiere with him and loved the movie, telling him, "I was so scared for my life and I'm so glad that we have each other now." Adele passed away four years later in July 2022.

_**I Can Only Imagine**_ is a 2018 American Christianbiographicaldrama film directed by the Erwin Brothers and written by Alex Cramer, Jon Erwin, and Brent McCorkle, based on the story behind the group MercyMe's song of the same name, one of the best-selling Christian singles of all time.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/I_Can_Only_Imagine_(film)#cite_note-5) The film stars J. Michael Finley as Bart Millard, the lead singer who wrote the song about his relationship with his father Arthur Millard (Dennis Quaid). Madeline Carroll, Trace Adkins, Priscilla Shirer, and Cloris Leachman also star.
_I Can Only Imagine_ was released in the United States on March 16, 2018. It was a box office success, grossing $86 million worldwide against a production budget of $7 million, earning more than twelve times its budget. It is the fifth highest-grossing music biopic[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/I_Can_Only_Imagine_(film)#cite_note-6) and sixth highest-grossing Christian film[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/I_Can_Only_Imagine_(film)#cite_note-7) of all-time in the United States. At the 2018 Dove Awards, the film won "Inspirational Film of the Year".[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/I_Can_Only_Imagine_(film)#cite_note-doveawards.com-8) A sequel, _I Can Only Imagine 2_, was released on February 20, 2026.
Ten-year-old Bart Millard lives with his mother Adele and abusive father Arthur in Texas. One day, Bart's mother drops him off at a Christian camp, where Bart meets Shannon Street. Upon his return from camp, Bart finds that his mother has left and movers are removing her belongings. Bart angrily confronts Arthur, who denies that his abusiveness was the reason she left.

Years later, in high school, Bart and Shannon are dating. Bart plays football to please Arthur, but is injured, breaking both ankles and ending his career. The only elective with openings is music class, so he reluctantly signs up. Initially, Bart is assigned to be a sound technician, but after overhearing him singing, the director casts him in the lead role in the school production of _Oklahoma!_. Bart overcomes his reluctance and gives an impressive performance, but does not tell Arthur, who finds out the night of the show when he happens to see a flyer for the show in a diner. Arthur suddenly collapses in pain, and finds out he has cancer, which he hides from Bart. The following morning, Bart fights with Arthur, who smashes a plate over his head. At church, Shannon sees the blood and presses Bart to open up, but he responds by breaking up with her, and leaves town to seek his fortune in the city.
Bart joins a band in need of a singer, and convinces Christian music producer Scott Brickell to manage the band and secure a showcase in Nashville. Bart surprises Shannon and invites her to tour with the band, and is confused when Shannon flatly refuses. In Nashville, Brickell introduces Bart to established artists Amy Grant and Michael W. Smith, but is unable to convince record executives to sign the band, who do not believe the band, now performing as "MercyMe", is good enough. Devastated, Bart quits the band, but Brickell thinks that Bart needs to resolve issues in his personal life, so Bart reconciles with the band and asks them to wait for him, and leaves to return home.
Bart returns home late at night, and is confused to find that Arthur has prepared breakfast for him the next morning. Arthur claims to have become a Christian, but Bart is skeptical and refuses to forgive him, and leaves. In anger and despair, Arthur smashes his old Jeep, which he had asked Bart to help him restore. Bart attempts to drive away in Arthur's pickup, but discovers his father's terminal cancer diagnosis, and returns to Arthur. Bart forgives his father, and the two form a deep bond, but Arthur soon dies of his illness.

After Arthur's funeral, Bart rejoins the band and writes "I Can Only Imagine", and also calls Shannon and apologizes to her for the first time since their breakup. Brickell sends the demo tape to several artists, including Grant, who, deeply moved by the song, asks to record it herself as her next single, and Bart, who just wants the song to be heard, accepts. On stage, Grant begins the song, but can't bring herself to sing it, and calls Bart on stage from the audience to sing it himself. After Bart's performance, he sees his father in the audience smiling and clapping. The audience gives an enthusiastic ovation, and he reunites with Shannon, who was also in attendance. The band releases the song as their first single, achieving success on both Christian and mainstream radio.

Michael Finley, who sang all the songs in the movie, makes his film debut as Bart Millard.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/I_Can_Only_Imagine_(film)#cite_note-deadline81417-1) The same month, it was announced that the film was slated for release in the spring of 2018.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/I_Can_Only_Imagine_(film)#cite_note-Deadline1517-10) In August 2017, Lionsgate and Roadside Attractions signed on as distributors for the film for a nationwide release in the United States.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/I_Can_Only_Imagine_(film)#cite_note-deadline81417-1)[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/I_Can_Only_Imagine_(film)#cite_note-11)
_I Can Only Imagine_ grossed $83.4 million in the United States and Canada and $1.8 million in other territories, for a worldwide total of $85.2 million, against a production budget of $7 million.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/I_Can_Only_Imagine_(film)#cite_note-TN-4) It is the highest-grossing independent film of 2018.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/I_Can_Only_Imagine_(film)#cite_note-12)

_I Can Only Imagine_ was released on March 16, 2018, alongside _Tomb Raider_ and _Love, Simon_, and was originally projected to gross $2–4 million from 1,620 theaters in its opening weekend.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/I_Can_Only_Imagine_(film)#cite_note-preview-13) However, after making $6.2 million on its first day (including $1.3 million from Thursday night previews), weekend estimates were increased to $14 million.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/I_Can_Only_Imagine_(film)#cite_note-opening-14) It ended up grossing $17.1 million, exceeding expectations and finishing third at the box office behind _Black Panther_ and _Tomb Raider_. 67% of the opening weekend audience was female while 80% was over the age of 35.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/I_Can_Only_Imagine_(film)#cite_note-opening2-15) It was the fourth best-ever opening for a faith-based film, following _The Passion of the Christ_ ($83.8 million), _Son of God_ ($25.6 million) and _Heaven Is for Real_ ($22.5 million).[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/I_Can_Only_Imagine_(film)#cite_note-16) In its second weekend the film was added to 624 additional theaters and dropped just 19% to $13.8 million, again finishing third.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/I_Can_Only_Imagine_(film)#cite_note-17) It was added to another 395 venues and finished fourth in its third weekend, making $10.4 million (including $3 million on Easter Sunday).[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/I_Can_Only_Imagine_(film)#cite_note-18)
The film has been translated and distributed in several countries,[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/I_Can_Only_Imagine_(film)#cite_note-19) including China, according to co-director Jon Erwin:

> I find it very interesting that in the same year that China actually restricted ... Christianity, they paid for "I Can Only Imagine". ... They paid for the right to translate it and distribute it to their people. That's happened in over 100 countries around the world with our films.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/I_Can_Only_Imagine_(film)#cite_note-20)
On review aggregatorRotten Tomatoes, the film holds an approval rating of 69% based on 32 reviews, with an average rating of 5.8/10. The website's critical consensus reads, "_I Can Only Imagine_'s message will have the most impact among Christian audiences, but overall, its performances and storytelling represent a notable evolution in faith-based cinema."[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/I_Can_Only_Imagine_(film)#cite_note-21) However, on Metacritic, the film has a weighted average score of 30 out of 100, based on eight critics, indicating "generally unfavorable" reviews.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/I_Can_Only_Imagine_(film)#cite_note-22) Audiences polled by CinemaScore gave the film a rare average grade of "A+" on an A+ to F scale.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/I_Can_Only_Imagine_(film)#cite_note-opening-14)

**Dennis Quaid** appears to be feeling happier than usual these days. No, not because he's playing the happy face killer, Keith Hunter Jesperson in the new Paramount+ limited series _Happy Face_. Nor because he starred in the Best Picture nominated horror film _The Substance_. But mainly that's because he's happily married to his wife, **Laura Savoie Quaid**, with whom he has been connected since 2019 and shares a production company.
**🎬****SIGN UP for Parade's Daily newsletter to get the latest pop culture news & celebrity interviews delivered right to your inbox****🎬**
But who exactly is Laura Savoie? Is she Quaid's first wife? How long have they been together? Do they have kids?
**Here is everything you need to know about Dennis Quaid's wife, Laura Savoie.**

## Who is Dennis Quaid married to?
_The Substance_ actor is currently married to Laura Savoie, 31. She is 39 years his junior, though their age gap is not even an issue to them. "There's 30-something years between us, and we just don't even notice it. I've never related to someone in my life better than we do," Quaidadmitted in a_Today_interview from 2020.
Savoie originated from St. Louis. She attended California-based Christian university, Pepperdine, where she went on to become class valedictorian. She then got her master's in accounting at the University of Notre Dame.

## How and when did Dennis Quaid meet his wife, Laura Savoie?
Quaid and Savoie met at a business event. They started dating in May 2019 when Savoie was studying for a PhD in accounting at the University of Texas at Austin's McCombs School of Business.
**Related:****Dennis Quaid's Son Jack's Bold Political Message Resurfaces After Famous Dad's Strong Statement**

## When did Dennis Quaid and Laura Savoie get engaged?
The _Happy Face_ actor and Savoie quickly got engaged a few months into dating. Quaid popped the question in Hawaii while he was shooting the **Roland Emmerich**action flick, _Midway_. "I had the ring in my pocket. It has been kind of a month-and-a-half plan—I wanted it to be private," Dennis shared with_Extra_in a press day interview for _Midway_. "She was actually taking a selfie of us, and I put the ring in front and said, 'Will you marry me?' And then she fell down."

## When did Dennis Quaid and Laura Savoie get married?
The couple were married on June 2, 2020, at a seaside resort in Santa Barbara. They were originally planning a Hawaiian wedding, but the COVID-19 pandemic complicated their plans. Only their pastor was a witness. "I've never met someone who is so in love with life," she saidin a_People_article regarding their wedding. "It's like nothing can bring him down. Just getting to do life with someone who lives that way is inspiring for me. It changes my perspective and it brings so much joy to every day."

## How many kids do Dennis Quaid and Laura Savoie have?
_The Parent Trap_ actor and Savoie don't share any kids together. However, they co-founded a film production company called Bonniedale Films. Their first production was the golf bio-drama _The Long Game_, which Quaid starred in.
**Related:****Dennis Quaid on His Latest Underdog Movie and Why He Makes a 'Great Team' with His Wife**

## What is Laura Savoie's occupation?
Savoie has held a variety of jobs. She's a registered yoga instructor, a real estate agent, a production company co-founder and a certified public accountant.

## Was Dennis Quaid previously married?
Yes, Savoie is _The Long Game_ star's fourth wife. He was first married to **P.J. Soles** from 1978 to 1983. Then Quaid married his _Innerspace_, _D.O.A._, and _Flesh and Bone_ co-star **Meg Ryan** from 1991 to 2001. They have a son together in _Novocaine_ star, **Jack Quaid**. Quaid married his third wife, **Kimberly Buffington**, in 2004, and had twin children, **Thomas** and **Zoe**, before eventually divorcing in 2018.

## What has Quaid said about his marriage to Savoie?
Quaid absolutely adores Savoie. They also have a shared interest in the Christian faith, which Quaid says is the key to their happy marriage. "God is in the relationship. I've never had a relationship like that before. I think you have to prepare a table for love and tend to it," Quaid elaborated to_People_. "That's what love is. That's what Laura and I have. I was ready to meet her, and I don't know why God had it that we met at the time that we did, but it's it for me. It's great."

When **Laura Savoie** married Hollywood actor Dennis Quaid in 2020, much of the public attention surrounding the couple focused on their **39-year age difference**. Yet her own story extends well beyond her marriage. Before entering the entertainment spotlight, Savoie had already developed an impressive background in accounting, corporate assurance, higher education and university teaching.
Today, she combines that financial experience with the entertainment industry as a **founding partner of Bonniedale Films**. Her professional journey includes **Pepperdine University, the University of Notre Dame, Ernst & Young (EY), the University of Texas at Austin**, and a producer credit on **The Long Game**, establishing a career identity separate from her husband’s fame.

| Field | Details |

## Academic Excellence and Early Career
Laura Savoie grew up in **St. Louis, Missouri**, and initially followed a professional path centered on business and accounting rather than entertainment. She attended **Pepperdine University**, where she completed her undergraduate accounting studies in three years and graduated in **2014 as valedictorian**.
She then continued her education at the **University of Notre Dame**, earning a **Master of Science in Accountancy in 2015**. Savoie graduated **magna cum laude**, adding another major academic achievement to an already distinguished educational record.
Her strong academic foundation eventually supported a career that moved between corporate accounting, university-level study and entertainment-business management.

## Ernst & Young Experience and Professional Credentials
After graduate school, Savoie entered the professional accounting sector and worked at **Ernst & Young (EY)** in Los Angeles between **2015 and 2017**. She worked within the firm’s assurance practice, gaining firsthand experience with financial reporting and business operations across several commercial industries.
Her professional exposure included clients in areas such as **real estate, biopharmaceuticals, retail consumer products, media and entertainment**. That experience placed her inside one of the world’s major accounting firms before she later moved into advanced academic study.
Savoie’s accounting credentials became particularly relevant later when she moved into film production, where budgeting, financial oversight and business planning are essential parts of developing entertainment projects.

## Doctoral Study and Teaching at Texas McCombs
Savoie eventually returned to academia at the **University of Texas at Austin’s McCombs School of Business**, where she pursued advanced study in accounting. During the period when her relationship with Dennis Quaid became public in 2019, she was deeply involved in doctoral-level academic work.
Her connection with McCombs was not limited to studying. In **summer 2019**, she served as an instructor for **Fundamentals of Financial Accounting**, a university course dealing with financial statements, business transactions and the interpretation of accounting information.
Her Texas McCombs experience included:
*   Advanced study in **accounting**  
*   University-level teaching responsibilities  
*   Teaching **Fundamentals of Financial Accounting**  
*   Applying her **CPA background** in an academic environment
This part of her career is especially notable because Savoie entered public life with professional and teaching experience already established, rather than building a career only after marrying a Hollywood celebrity.

## How Laura Savoie Met Dennis Quaid
Laura Savoie and **Dennis Quaid met in 2019 at a business event** after being introduced through a mutual connection. At the time, Savoie was involved in graduate accounting study and teaching, while Quaid was already an internationally recognized actor with several decades of film experience.
Their relationship progressed quickly. Quaid has described their connection as **“love at first sight”** and has often emphasized Savoie’s intelligence, personality and shared values when discussing why their relationship became serious so quickly.
The relationship also placed Savoie under far greater public attention than she had previously experienced. Before meeting Quaid, her public identity had largely been centered around **education, accounting and professional achievement** rather than entertainment coverage.

## Engagement and Wedding at San Ysidro Ranch
Dennis Quaid proposed to Laura Savoie during a trip to **Oahu, Hawaii, in October 2019**. The proposal occurred while the couple were taking a photograph together, with Quaid surprising her with the engagement ring during what initially appeared to be an ordinary moment.
The couple originally planned a larger wedding in Hawaii for **April 2020**, followed by another celebration in Nashville. The COVID-19 pandemic disrupted those plans, leading them to arrange a much smaller ceremony instead.
Important details from their wedding include:
*   Engagement took place in **Oahu, Hawaii**  
*   Quaid proposed in **October 2019**  
*   Original Hawaii wedding plans were disrupted in 2020  
*   They married on **June 2, 2020**  
*   Ceremony took place at **San Ysidro Ranch**  
*   Their pastor was present as the witness
Savoie wore a bridal gown by **Chosen By One Day**, while Quaid wore a light gray Hugo Boss suit. The intimate Santa Barbara ceremony became a considerably more private beginning to their marriage than the larger destination celebration they had originally planned.

## Marriage, Family Life and Their 39-Year Age Difference
Laura Savoie and Dennis Quaid have a **39-year age difference**, which became one of the most discussed aspects of their relationship after their engagement became public. Quaid was born in **1954**, while Savoie is 33 years old in 2026.
Despite the public interest surrounding their ages, Quaid has consistently treated the difference as secondary to their compatibility. He has described Savoie as one of the closest relationships of his life and has emphasized that their age difference does not dominate their everyday marriage.
Savoie also became part of Quaid’s larger family. Dennis Quaid has three children from earlier marriages: actor **Jack Quaid** and twins **Thomas Boone Quaid and Zoe Grace Quaid**.
Savoie is Quaid’s fourth wife. His previous marriages were to **P.J. Soles, Meg Ryan and Kimberly Buffington**. Her relationship with his family forms one part of a marriage that also includes faith, travel, music and their growing professional partnership.

The veteran actor and his wife stepped out together for an L.A. screening of his new film 'The Long Game'
By
Julia Moore

Dennis Quaid and his wife Laura Savoie turned the red carpet into a date night!
On April 10, _The Parent Trap_ star stepped out for a screening of his latest film, _The Long Game_, with his wife in Los Angeles just one day after celebrating his 70th birthday.
The actor was looking smart in a leather jacket, button-down shirt and pants, while Savoie, 30, bared some skin in a one-shoulder black top with a cutout on her midriff, along with a pair of classic white trousers.
_The Long Game_, which also stars Jay Hernandez, Brett Cullen and Oscar Nuñez, sees Quaid help JB Peña (Hernandez) start a golf team for Mexican-American kids after facing discrimination in Texas. The film, based on Humberto G. Garcia's 2010 novel, _Mustang Miracle_, tells the true story of how Peña's group of high schoolers made history with their victory in the 1957 Texas state golf championship. The film originally premiered at SXSW in 2023, and Savoie joined Quaid on the red carpet for the debut, as well.

# Dennis Quaid Makes Red Carpet Appearance with Wife Laura Savoie Days After 70th Birthday
The veteran actor and his wife stepped out together for an L.A. screening of his new film 'The Long Game'
By
Julia Moore
Julia Moore
Julia Moore is a TV Writer-Reporter at PEOPLE. She has been working at PEOPLE since 2022.
People Editorial Guidelines
Published on April 11, 2024 09:54AM EDT
Add Us On
Dennis Quaid (L) and Laura Savoie (R) attend a screening of 'The Long Game' in Los Angeles on April 10.Credit :   
Scott Kirkland/Shutterstock
Dennis Quaid and his wife Laura Savoie turned the red carpet into a date night!
On April 10, _The Parent Trap_ star stepped out for a screening of his latest film, _The Long Game_, with his wife in Los Angeles just one day after celebrating his 70th birthday.
The actor was looking smart in a leather jacket, button-down shirt and pants, while Savoie, 30, bared some skin in a one-shoulder black top with a cutout on her midriff, along with a pair of classic white trousers.
_The Long Game_, which also stars Jay Hernandez, Brett Cullen and Oscar Nuñez, sees Quaid help JB Peña (Hernandez) start a golf team for Mexican-American kids after facing discrimination in Texas. The film, based on Humberto G. Garcia's 2010 novel, _Mustang Miracle_, tells the true story of how Peña's group of high schoolers made history with their victory in the 1957 Texas state golf championship. The film originally premiered at SXSW in 2023, and Savoie joined Quaid on the red carpet for the debut, as well.

Last year, the actor raved to PEOPLE about his wife, who he met in 2019 and married in secret a year later, describing their life together as "heaven."

When **Laura Savoie** married Hollywood actor Dennis Quaid in 2020, much of the public attention surrounding the couple focused on their **39-year age difference**. Yet her own story extends well beyond her marriage. Before entering the entertainment spotlight, Savoie had already developed an impressive background in accounting, corporate assurance, higher education and university teaching.
Today, she combines that financial experience with the entertainment industry as a **founding partner of Bonniedale Films**. Her professional journey includes **Pepperdine University, the University of Notre Dame, Ernst & Young (EY), the University of Texas at Austin**, and a producer credit on **The Long Game**, establishing a career identity separate from her husband’s fame.

## Academic Excellence and Early Career
Laura Savoie grew up in **St. Louis, Missouri**, and initially followed a professional path centered on business and accounting rather than entertainment. She attended **Pepperdine University**, where she completed her undergraduate accounting studies in three years and graduated in **2014 as valedictorian**.
She then continued her education at the **University of Notre Dame**, earning a **Master of Science in Accountancy in 2015**. Savoie graduated **magna cum laude**, adding another major academic achievement to an already distinguished educational record.
Her strong academic foundation eventually supported a career that moved between corporate accounting, university-level study and entertainment-business management.
texts.3:
## Ernst & Young Experience and Professional Credentials
After graduate school, Savoie entered the professional accounting sector and worked at **Ernst & Young (EY)** in Los Angeles between **2015 and 2017**. She worked within the firm’s assurance practice, gaining firsthand experience with financial reporting and business operations across several commercial industries.
Her professional exposure included clients in areas such as **real estate, biopharmaceuticals, retail consumer products, media and entertainment**. That experience placed her inside one of the world’s major accounting firms before she later moved into advanced academic study.
Savoie’s accounting credentials became particularly relevant later when she moved into film production, where budgeting, financial oversight and business planning are essential parts of developing entertainment projects.
texts.4:
## Doctoral Study and Teaching at Texas McCombs
Savoie eventually returned to academia at the **University of Texas at Austin’s McCombs School of Business**, where she pursued advanced study in accounting. During the period when her relationship with Dennis Quaid became public in 2019, she was deeply involved in doctoral-level academic work.
Her connection with McCombs was not limited to studying. In **summer 2019**, she served as an instructor for **Fundamentals of Financial Accounting**, a university course dealing with financial statements, business transactions and the interpretation of accounting information.
Her Texas McCombs experience included:
*   Advanced study in **accounting**  
*   University-level teaching responsibilities  
*   Teaching **Fundamentals of Financial Accounting**  
*   Applying her **CPA background** in an academic environment
This part of her career is especially notable because Savoie entered public life with professional and teaching experience already established, rather than building a career only after marrying a Hollywood celebrity.
texts.5:
## How Laura Savoie Met Dennis Quaid
Laura Savoie and **Dennis Quaid met in 2019 at a business event** after being introduced through a mutual connection. At the time, Savoie was involved in graduate accounting study and teaching, while Quaid was already an internationally recognized actor with several decades of film experience.
Their relationship progressed quickly. Quaid has described their connection as **“love at first sight”** and has often emphasized Savoie’s intelligence, personality and shared values when discussing why their relationship became serious so quickly.
The relationship also placed Savoie under far greater public attention than she had previously experienced. Before meeting Quaid, her public identity had largely been centered around **education, accounting and professional achievement** rather than entertainment coverage.
texts.6:
## Engagement and Wedding at San Ysidro Ranch
Dennis Quaid proposed to Laura Savoie during a trip to **Oahu, Hawaii, in October 2019**. The proposal occurred while the couple were taking a photograph together, with Quaid surprising her with the engagement ring during what initially appeared to be an ordinary moment.
The couple originally planned a larger wedding in Hawaii for **April 2020**, followed by another celebration in Nashville. The COVID-19 pandemic disrupted those plans, leading them to arrange a much smaller ceremony instead.
Important details from their wedding include:
*   Engagement took place in **Oahu, Hawaii**  
*   Quaid proposed in **October 2019**  
*   Original Hawaii wedding plans were disrupted in 2020  
*   They married on **June 2, 2020**  
*   Ceremony took place at **San Ysidro Ranch**  
*   Their pastor was present as the witness
Savoie wore a bridal gown by **Chosen By One Day**, while Quaid wore a light gray Hugo Boss suit. The intimate Santa Barbara ceremony became a considerably more private beginning to their marriage than the larger destination celebration they had originally planned.
texts.7:
## Marriage, Family Life and Their 39-Year Age Difference
Laura Savoie and Dennis Quaid have a **39-year age difference**, which became one of the most discussed aspects of their relationship after their engagement became public. Quaid was born in **1954**, while Savoie is 33 years old in 2026.
Despite the public interest surrounding their ages, Quaid has consistently treated the difference as secondary to their compatibility. He has described Savoie as one of the closest relationships of his life and has emphasized that their age difference does not dominate their everyday marriage.
Savoie also became part of Quaid’s larger family. Dennis Quaid has three children from earlier marriages: actor **Jack Quaid** and twins **Thomas Boone Quaid and Zoe Grace Quaid**.
Savoie is Quaid’s fourth wife. His previous marriages were to **P.J. Soles, Meg Ryan and Kimberly Buffington**. Her relationship with his family forms one part of a marriage that also includes faith, travel, music and their growing professional partnership.

Dennis Quaid and his wife Laura Savoie turned the red carpet into a date night!
On April 10, _The Parent Trap_ star stepped out for a screening of his latest film, _The Long Game_, with his wife in Los Angeles just one day after celebrating his 70th birthday.
The actor was looking smart in a leather jacket, button-down shirt and pants, while Savoie, 30, bared some skin in a one-shoulder black top with a cutout on her midriff, along with a pair of classic white trousers.
_The Long Game_, which also stars Jay Hernandez, Brett Cullen and Oscar Nuñez, sees Quaid help JB Peña (Hernandez) start a golf team for Mexican-American kids after facing discrimination in Texas. The film, based on Humberto G. Garcia's 2010 novel, _Mustang Miracle_, tells the true story of how Peña's group of high schoolers made history with their victory in the 1957 Texas state golf championship. The film originally premiered at SXSW in 2023, and Savoie joined Quaid on the red carpet for the debut, as well.

He told PEOPLE he's learned “to let go of a lot of things," which has helped pave the way for his and Savoie's love story.
"I think you have to prepare a table for love and tend to it. That’s what love is," he continued. “That’s what Laura and I have. I was ready to meet her, and I don’t know why God had it that we met at the time that we did, but it’s it for me. It’s great."
